4.1.2. RADIAL BASIS FUNCTIONS
We take m = 2, such that we will calculate two radial basis functions. We set the initial centers of
the RBFs to be close to optimal using a k-means clustering algorithm and allow the widths of our
RBF to be chosen arbitrarily. We take γ = 0.25 to be the threshold of our RBF, N = 1000 samples,
and β = 10−9. The output of Algorithm 2 for this problem, which took approximately 7 minutes to
